title: Capital structure
question: What is authorised and paid-up capital?

body.normal: Authorised capital is the most share capital the company may issue under its MOA. Paid-up capital is the part the subscribers actually pay for their shares at incorporation.
body.simple: Authorised capital is the upper limit; paid-up capital is the money actually put in for shares.
body.detail: The capital clause of the Memorandum of Association states the authorised capital and how it divides into shares of a face value, for example 10,000 shares of ₹10 each. The subscribers take some or all of those shares at incorporation and pay for them after the bank account opens; that amount is the paid-up capital. Authorised capital can be increased later, but government fees at incorporation depend on it.
body.why: These numbers go into the MOA, the subscription sheet and the share certificates, and they decide how much money has to reach the company's bank account.
